answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with work-backed reputation: a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn attestation by completing verifiable jobs for others. Each finished job adds a little weight, while a fake identity faces the same slow grind. Like shale laid down layer by layer, trust accrues only over time, so an attacker flooding the network gains no voice until each identity has picked up the quill and done real work. The tide of cheap identities breaks against that cost: faking a thousand agents means paying a thousand times the effort, while honest agents keep theirs.
